title: The Axeman of New Orleans: Who Spared the City With Jazz? (1918-1919 Unsolved)
description:
Between May 1918 and October 1919, New Orleans lived in terror of a killer who broke into homes through chiseled door panels, always targeting Italian grocers, always leaving the axe behind. Joseph and Catherine Maggio were the first — found dead in bed, no forced lock, no witnesses. Six more attacks followed the same eerie pattern.

The case turned bizarre when a letter signed 'the Axeman' appeared in the Times-Picayune, claiming demonic origins and promising to spare any home playing jazz at 12:15 a.m. on March 19, 1919. The city complied, filling the night with music — but the killings continued. Two-year-old Mary Cortimiglia was murdered, her parents wounded, and survivor Rosie Cortimiglia's accusations sent two innocent neighbors to prison before she recanted.

Mike Pepitone became the final confirmed victim in October 1919. Over a year later, his widow shot a man in Los Angeles she swore was the Axeman — but no fingerprint, confession, or trial ever confirmed his identity. To this day, nobody knows who wrote that letter, or why the killings simply stopped.
